The shared memory tiling paid off nicely. Here's the summary:

**Final results** — [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p42/round0/output_model_new.py)

The kernel uses a 16×16 output tile with a 19×19 shared memory input tile (cooperatively loaded by all 256 threads in the block). Each thread then computes the max over its 4×4 kernel window entirely from shared memory, avoiding the redundant global memory reads that the naive version suffered from. The stride-1, kernel_size-4 problem happens to be a sweet spot for this tiling strategy — each input element feeds up to 16 output elements, so the shared memory cache cuts global memory traffic dramatically.
